summary.headline: Suryoday SFB FY26 PAT rose to ₹152 crores from ₹115 crores; management targets FY27 PAT above ₹300 crores, with credit cost guided at 70-80 bps.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of disciplined execution and gradual stabilisation after elevated microfinance credit costs. Q4 showed improvement: inclusive finance slippages fell to about ₹74 crores from ₹116 crores in Q3 (the call also cited ₹106 crores on a total-bank basis), and monthly disbursements returned to about ₹500 crores. FY26 net total income rose 10.2% to ₹1,458 crores and PAT to ₹152 crores, with GNPA at 6.5% (₹864 crores) and CRAR at 20.5%. Management guided to 30%+ growth, a 1.2% ROA for Q1 FY27 rising to 1.6% by Q4, and a cost-to-income ratio of 67-68%.

financial_highlights.value: ₹542 crores, of which ₹508 crores receivable from CGFMU

financial_highlights.metric: Mortgage book incl. micro home loans (Mar'26)

segments.name: Inclusive finance (microfinance)
segments.commentary: Shifting from JLG to individual Vikas loans, now 75% of the inclusive finance portfolio and growing about 40-45% YoY. Current-book collection efficiency is about 99.7%; slippages were about ₹74 crores in Q4 versus ₹116 crores in Q3.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Portfolio ₹1,819 crores, up 36% YoY. Stress is concentrated in an Odisha pocket; management says ex-Odisha metrics are about 2x better than market CV stress.

segments.name: Mortgages and micro home loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage book ₹3,013 crores, up 38% YoY. Stress in older mortgage and MHL portfolios in Karnataka was about 4% of the portfolio, with a few high-ticket LAP cases (₹3 crores+) in SARFAESI resolution.

segments.name: Digital products (credit on UPI, secured cards, digital MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Credit on UPI outstanding about ₹200 crores with 97-98% of dues paid; 90+ DPD about 1.5%. Of 10 lakh prequalified customers, about 5.5 lakh sanctioned and about 3 lakh utilised.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 ROA guided at about 1.2%, rising to 1.6% by Q4 FY27; Q4 FY26 ROA was 1.1%.
FY27 PAT target above ₹300 crores (about 2x FY26), per management's presentation.
FY27 credit cost of about 1%, per CFO earlier in the call; later revised to 70-80 bps for the coming year (FY27) in response to a follow-up question.
Cost-to-income ratio of 67-68% for FY27, with a stated goal of staying below 70%.
Quarterly slippages targeted at ₹75-90 crores; GNPA guided to about 3% for FY27 with CGFMU claims and write-offs as the main drivers.
NIM to be range-bound at 8-9%, with an uptick possible as the paying book grows; current NIM about 50 bps suppressed. Growth targeted at 20-30% of asset size.
capex_capacity: CGFMU claims: about ₹510 crores claimable, of which about ₹450 crores (up to ₹475 crores) is expected in FY27; the first cohort claim is targeted for Q1 or Q2, with the FY25 cohort the largest.
CGFMU cover premium expected at about ₹100-110 crores for FY27 (about ₹23 crores per quarter currently).
Fundraise: Tier 2 is the likely first step, possibly within FY27. An equity raise is more contingent, given the stock trades below book (P/B under 1) and the need to protect incumbent shareholders.
Branch expansion is kept rationalised and low-cost; corporate headcount is held flat, with hiring concentrated in frontline roles.
demand_pricing: Digital deposits are about 50% of net incremental deposit flows, with average ticket about ₹1.25 lakh and at least two deposits per customer on average.
Cost of funds has hardened; elevated Q4 rates have not come down as in prior years. The bank uses a mix of deposits and refinancing lines to manage funding.
Management sees unmet demand as large, especially where smaller MFIs have exited; the top 10-15 MFIs hold about 19% market share.
Individual-loan ticket sizes are being raised selectively; tenor is moving toward 3 years for high-ticket loans, with a portion above ₹1 lakh under review.

qa_highlights.question: Given the stronger Q4 performance, is the 1.2% Q1 ROA target realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said yes: the paying book is higher entering Q1, impaired book should exit on CGFMU claims, and Q1 typically has the most PSLC sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state slippage level and retail-asset (RA) slippage guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said RA slippage could settle near 1.25% over the next two halves as CV Odisha stress and high-ticket mortgage cases are resolved. Bank-wide slippages are targeted at ₹75-90 crores a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the CGFMU claim will be filed, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹510 crores is claimable, with ₹450 crores expected in FY27 and the timing (Q1 or Q2) still open. None filed in April; May is unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank raising capital, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is raising capital to sustain 30%+ growth, with CRAR around 20% as the internal comfort level. Tier 2 is most likely first, and an equity raise is subject to shareholder considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIMs expand as the paying book grows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided NIM to 8-9% and agreed NIM is suppressed by about 50 bps, with an uptick expected as non-paying assets convert to paying.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be expected for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided FY27 credit cost to 70-80 bps. Management also said downside risk from the Middle East war and diesel prices would be watched, with CV impact only if diesel rises above 10-15%.

risks_watch: Odisha CV stress and high-ticket mortgage slippages; RA book slippage about 1.8% in Q4.
Credit card and UPI products (CLOU): the customer relationship is shared with One97 (Paytm); ownership is being clarified offline. Early 90+ DPD about 1.5%.
Diesel price increases above 10-15% could hit large CV fleet operators; indirect MSME impact on mortgages from the war.
State-level loan waivers (farm and MFI) could cause localised stress; management cites Maharashtra pockets such as Kolhapur and Nagpur.
Rising cost of deposits, deposit growth below guidance, and dependence on digital platforms (not on one or two).
Equity dilution risk versus price-to-book below 1; Tier 2 capital is the preferred first step.
Timing of CGFMU claims and whether FY25 cohort is claimed in Q1 or Q2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 trends and FY27 targets, but cautious on macro risks such as the war, diesel and monsoon, and noncommittal on fundraising timing and equity dilution. Management was candid about the Odisha and mortgage stress and stated that the 1.2% ROA guidance reflects about 90% confidence.
key_quotes: We did not burn all the candles in Q4.
So we currently see a traction which is around closer to 50% of our incremental deposits, which is completely granular.
So I would say that it is a little more realistic. If there's any upside, it will be good.
So the goal is to come below 70% for sure.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 PAT above ₹300 crores (about 2x FY26's ₹152 crores), loan growth of 20-30%, and ROA rising from 1.2% in Q1 FY27 to 1.6% by Q4, but the backing is largely demand recovery, collection efficiency and CGFMU claims with no specific new capacity, orders or contracts quantified.
